chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Imran ibn Ali al-Halbi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When does the 'Atamah (Isha prayer) become obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When the twilight disappears.' And the twilight is the redness. So Ubaydullah said, 'May Allah keep you well! After the disappearance of the redness, a strong light remains, crossing [the sky].' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, the twilight is only the redness, and the light is not from the twilight.'

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: Twilight, specifically the redness in the sky after sunset
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: The redness, identified by the Imam as the true definition of shafaq
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةُ: The 'Atamah, referring to the late Isha prayer
key_terms.ضَوْءٌ شَدِيدٌ: Strong light, referring to the white light that remains after the redness fades

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of twilight (shafaq) for the time of Isha prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise astronomical definition of 'shafaq' for the onset of the 'Atamah (late Isha) prayer, distinguishing the red twilight glow from the residual white light. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh for determining the end of the Maghrib time window and the beginning of the extended Isha period, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on precise celestial observation. The narration highlights the Imam's role in refining legal definitions based on observable natural phenomena.
